chemistry_scientist.state_summary: The current packet contains 717 observed records, 2,613 eligible candidate records, no pending experiments, and no validation or test records. The current observed table supersedes the embedded round-11 summaries where counts or mappings differ. Overall retrained Row V1/V2 accuracy remains unverified.

important_observations.statement: m177 is an exceptional, strongly non-smooth surface. At 50/1, V2 is 59.88, 7.31 and 81.30 ml at 50, 100 and 150 ul. At 100 ul, V2 is 19.18, 20.70 and 7.31 ml at 5/1, 10/1 and 50/1; V1 remains near 5 ml. The measured 5/1, 50 ul and 20/1, 50 ul points are 14.51 and 8.50 ml in V2. These observations reject simple loading interpolation. A reproducible conditional minimum and omitted experimental variation remain competing hypotheses.

m194 changes response shape with loading. At 100 ul, completion decreases from 36.18 to 28.27 ml between 1/1 and 2/1 with nearly fixed onset. At 50 ul, the corresponding measured sequence is 10.34, 14.73 and 21.52 ml at 1/1, 2/1 and 5/1. A common ratio correction or monotone loading term is inadequate.

The corrected fixed-50 ul m20 curve rises from 7.70/10.73 at 1/1 to 10.80/15.09 at 2/1, 15.84/22.69 at 5/1 and 23.78/34.90 at 10/1. The previously attributed low-ratio observation was m148, so the actual m20 baseline is now measured and the earlier shoulder interpretation is rejected.

m106 now has a connected fixed-100 ul sequence: 6.23/10.54, 7.16/13.39, 20.86/42.52 and 41.72/79.81 ml at 1/1, 2/1, 10/1 and 20/1. This supports a delayed joint transition in an ether-containing ketone, while the historical 10/1 prediction substantially overstated both endpoints.

Aminoester transfer is local. m86 and m88 show substantial joint endpoint growth by 5/1 under their fixed 100 ul DCM conditions, whereas m89 remains moderate through 10/1 under PE loading and m104 has a moderate 5/1-to-10/1 response. Different loading solvent, plug volume, density and substitution environment prevent attributing the contrast to amino position alone.

Alcohol response is heterogeneous: fixed-50 ul m60 grows strongly with ratio, while fixed-100 ul m61 onset decreases from 12.34 to 3.04 ml across 2/1 to 10/1. The m61 50 ul pair shows a much smaller change. A shared alcohol correction is unsupported.

Identical m92 1/1, 50 ul, EA-loaded inputs give 5.18/12.01 and 5.72/11.70 ml, while the single PE-loaded counterpart gives 8.02/20.57 ml. This supports local persistence of the short EA completion, but PE-side repeatability and a general solvent-identity effect remain untested.

Increasing EA fraction generally strengthens normal-phase silica elution. Donor accessibility, basic nitrogen, hydrogen bonding, injection-solvent focusing and adsorption can modify this locally. These are chemical priors and are not established causes of any measured anomaly.

possible_model_blind_spots.statement: A single molecular offset, global loading term or smooth monotone ratio interpolation cannot represent the m177, m194 and m61 surfaces. V1 and V2 need separate molecule-by-condition interactions.

Functional-group counts and broad polarity descriptors do not reliably transfer response shapes: aminoesters, alcohols, ether carbonyls and beta-ketoesters with similar HBD/HBA patterns occupy different regimes.

Some current candidate outputs have non-monotone or incoherent predicted quantiles, including q50 values outside the q10-to-q90 ordering. This indicates output-calibration or representation issues, but quantile width is not measured uncertainty and does not establish expected learning value.

Loading amount, sample volume, loading-solvent identity, plug volume and density are strongly entangled in the pool. A model may learn spurious global effects unless these are represented as conditional features and evaluated with matched complete tuples.

The adaptively sampled pool is rich in exceptional high-tail surfaces. Overall Row accuracy may still be limited by ordinary moderate-response chemistry and lower-ratio condition coverage; historical residual magnitude alone cannot establish Row prevalence.

warnings: Only observed-table records are measured evidence. Candidate IDs and all candidate endpoint values are predictions only.
Historical prediction errors describe prior acquisition behavior and are not current candidate error or current Row error.
V2 minus V1 is an elution interval width, not uncertainty.
Exact duplicate candidate tuples should be collapsed unless a named repeatability question justifies repetition. Candidate multiplicity does not establish prevalence.

The m177, m207 and m120 exceptional measurements remain difficult to interpret mechanistically. Adsorption, focusing, solubility, local silica interactions and omitted experimental variables are hypotheses, not findings.
The current objective is retrained overall Row V1/V2 accuracy. Chromatographic desirability, narrow intervals or large predicted endpoints are not acquisition objectives.

particularly_informative_candidates.reason: Connected lower-ratio m177 conditions can test response-shape continuity while preserving the warning that they do not replicate the exceptional high-ratio minima.
A lower-ratio, higher-loading m194 point provides a chemically interpretable loading/mobile-phase contrast after opposite response shapes were observed at 50 and 100 ul.
This ordinary m114 lower-ratio point adds a missing moderate-response anchor and helps distinguish general condition smoothing from tail-specific behavior.

The current catalog and latest measured feedback favor specific condition-response and structural-transfer questions. Several previous gaps are now answered, including the actual m20 baseline. ml_scientist.important_observations:
H24 is supported with narrower transfer. Observed m89 e513420e1b7414424e7c and 693a65467095367c8e95 grow from 8.81/14.05 at 5/1 to 13.49/26.04 ml at 10/1,100 ul. Observed m104 645cb06b9e2a33b6044b and 467ccfac002f5113fe81 instead change from 5.20/13.90 to 7.91/11.00: onset grows while completion falls. Observed m86 c70b471334f9747d6f98 and 9bc73e0c27d4d6b44abb retain steep 5/1 response across loading, but full endpoint invariance is rejected. Increasing sample volume from 50 to 150 ul changes endpoints by -5.25/-1.31 ml. Completion is comparatively stable while onset advances. These prior questions are substantially answered; cross-molecule differences still include injection-context differences.
H18 requires revision. Observed m194 c0094343ab6bb16bc58b, 2bd4f8787a951ef0ee04 and c393010c592b487413e2 have fixed-50 ul completion 10.34/14.73/21.52 ml across 1/1,2/1,5/1. Transfer of the measured 100 ul completion decline is rejected. At 100 ul, observed 4a39c1f64d17e050e4a5 and 66c6a533f485d5277f2f instead decrease from 36.18 to 28.27 between 1/1 and 2/1. The 50-to-100 ul completion differences are +25.84 and +13.54 ml at those ratios, with much smaller onset changes. This supports a loading-dependent response shape without establishing repeatability.
The actual m20 baseline gap is repaired: observed 66e8febca8812396280d and 3b41addf80b8138137db measure 7.70/10.73 at 1/1 and 10.80/15.09 at 2/1,50 ul, connecting to its measured increasing 5/1 and 10/1 curve. The older 66e712388ecd53b9c22c remains an m148 record. For m106, observed 7155ede91e7e3232862a measures 20.86/42.52 at 10/1 before measured 20/1 reaches 41.72/79.81. Its historical 10/1 forecast placed substantial growth too early, indicating a response-shape failure rather than a constant offset.
H13 gains qualified support. Observed m61 e71aba5ca322ce0a2c7f and f15b726ca5b4897ed80c show an onset decrease of only 2.32 ml from 2/1 to 10/1 at 50 ul, versus 9.30 ml at 100 ul from observed f559a4634c60d81f5f15 and 859ae738b615cf17b849. Completion decreases similarly at both loadings: 4.63 versus 4.75 ml. Thus the inverse onset response persists qualitatively, but its strong loading-invariant form is rejected. The difference between ratio effects is approximately -6.98 ml for V1 and -0.12 for V2. Exceptional m120/m207 inputs remain unreplicated.
H15 is refined. Observed m25 ec1c29d6d4fe334c886a, 3b6524f5fc7e0343ff9b and d21f08a7e8eaa163ecfc grow jointly through 2/1,5/1,10/1 at 100 ul, reaching 12.19/25.05, far below observed 50/1 at 42.22/88.03. Observed m82 5b7151c95c4e964a121b reaches 18.61/46.04 at 10/1,150 ul; m95 41f57dc6d50ee162801a reaches 16.78/33.73 at 10/1,50 ul. Their historical completion errors at 10/1 were +27.51,-19.35,-8.76 ml respectively. Opposite errors reject a shared beta-ketoester correction; different injections prevent isolated attribution to ester alkyl groups.
H25's initial curve questions are substantially answered. Observed m45 77aca3cfa4edafa6e181, fc47eff9bc6b7be6c207 and d43d692e19100ebe5646 grow jointly from 6.02/9.46 at 1/1 to 14.79/32.17 at 10/1,100 ul. Observed m96 fa81c4e1817366c902f3 and 376ba323d8d487f80cee connect its 2/1-to-20/1 growth at fixed 150 ul. These broaden donor-environment evidence without establishing a shared donor correction.
H17's lactone question narrows. Observed m181 4a565c53862a9a8c3de3, eedc2caf00196610c74d and 2cc7c8ae52cdb25ca284 measure 6.18/10.19,7.38/13.29,21.45/31.79 at 1/1,2/1,10/1,50 ul. A large early completion tail is unsupported; substantial later growth involves both endpoints. Compared with observed 64c9e190e213bb061867, increasing loading to 150 ul at 10/1 changes V1/V2 by -3.47/+0.33 ml.
ml_scientist.important_model_behaviors:
Current predictions show local adaptation after large historical errors. Candidate duplicate 6f3dff9a427ee1563a3e predicts m25 5/1,100 ul at 8.46/15.47 versus observed 3b6524f5fc7e0343ff9b at 8.47/15.77. Candidate duplicate b6ffd4ffa7739deb3e88 predicts m82 10/1,150 ul at 19.72/45.18 versus observed 5b7151c95c4e964a121b at 18.61/46.04. These are fit diagnostics using existing labels; the candidate IDs themselves remain unmeasured. Local fit is uneven: m89 duplicate 5df4935254e8c1e8471d predicts completion 17.28 at an input whose observed completion is 14.05.
Previously cited quantile defects at m29 60880ddea87941f6e9ca and m155 b213664a8c509420288b are now ordered. Other crossings remain: m62 6553b9607d6093f257c7 has V1 q50/q90 of 5.86/5.30, and m45 129036e0bccc4ff7e848 has V2 q50/q90 of 73.01/72.03. Zero V1 q10 values also make widths strongly dependent on endpoint scale. Positive width does not imply coherent or calibrated uncertainty.
Point-endpoint reversals occur in current m18 8e17cb06a37c48cc9ab5 at 4.13/3.96 and m71 c3070604fe243a9e8bc9 at 5.61/4.62 ml. The original m13/m80 anomaly premise remains rejected; these are separate current output defects, without measured evidence of reversed elution. They do not automatically justify acquisition.
Predicted loading effects remain nearly flat in many families. For example, m82 10/1 predictions differ by only about 0.04/0.05 ml between 50 and 150 ul. Such invariance may be locally correct, but measured m61,m86,m181 show why V1 and V2 need separate interpretation.
ml_scientist.possible_model_blind_spots: Inference from measured contrasts: common molecular offsets, functional-group corrections and global loading terms cannot describe the endpoint-specific associations in m194,m61,m86 and the older m177 surface. Similar descriptors do not establish matching response curves. ML prior: interaction-aware representations and coherent endpoint/quantile parameterizations may help, but their Row benefit is unverified. Adsorption, focusing, solubility, intramolecular hydrogen bonding and tautomerism remain untested chemical explanations.
ml_scientist.possible_learning_bottlenecks: The packet cannot distinguish feature representation, regularization, optimization and omitted experimental variables as causes of conditional smoothing. Audit training-only fit by molecule, ratio, loading and endpoint before assuming more nearby labels will solve every error. Audit raw outputs, transformations and serialization for endpoint and quantile inconsistencies without spending labels. Global monotonicity in ratio or loading is unsupported by these measured surfaces. Replicate-aware analysis should separate repeated-input variation from new-condition residuals; unusual singleton labels should neither be automatically discarded nor treated as deterministic.
ml_scientist.coverage_or_redundancy_concerns: Current catalog diagnostics report molecular novelty zero and maximum observed similarity 1.0 throughout the supplied candidate rows. Exploration therefore concerns condition coverage and less sampled surfaces within observed identities. Molecular familiarity does not establish condition-response coverage. Full-tuple duplicates remain extensive: m69 3584971523a9f99cac5c and 686cce1ee0199615cff5 are identical inputs; m75 dccd8753d89546cbf994 and ef8724fc040ffeca44b7 are another pair. Assess diversity using molecule plus all five condition fields. Multiplicity does not establish Row prevalence. Routine expansion of completed m86 loading,m89 moderate-ratio,m20 baseline,m45/m96 and older m28,m125,m167,m173,m212 surfaces has diminishing value. Boundary predictions alone do not reopen rejected m80-transition or m68-rebound expectations.
ml_scientist.candidate_scientific_questions: Useful remaining distinctions include whether m194's 1/1 completion transfers to 150 ul; where m61's onset decrease appears at 150 ul; where m25's later growth begins; and whether ordinary ether-acrylate, conjugated aminoester and nitro-alcohol curves transfer from measured analogues. New conditions constrain response shape. They cannot resolve reproducibility of exceptional m177,m120 or m207 inputs.
